newsitem.title: USA: Ascend stock rises on upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Ascend stock rises on upgrade.

text.p: Ascend Communications Inc.'s stock rose in active trading Wednesday on positive comments by two Wall Street firms amid rumours of at least one impending multimillion-dollar pact with an Internet service provider.
Ascend rose for a second consecutive day, ending $5.31 higher at $49.06 on Nasdaq, where it was the most active issue on volume of 20.6 million shares. The stock has risen 24 percent since Monday.
Merrill Lynch & Co., which had previously rated the stock neutral, on Wednesday upgraded it to accumulate for intermediate gains. No further details were available.
On Tuesday, Montgomery Securities made positive comments about the company's upcoming second-quarter earnings.
Ascend, based in Alameda, Calif., makes computer network equipment for telecommunications carriers, Internet service providers and corporate customers.

"I heard that Ascend won a big deal at UUNET, that's all I know," said David Takata, a Gruntal & Co. analyst. UUNET, one of the largest Internet service providers and now owned by WorldCom Inc., is believed to have picked Ascend's networking products over Cisco Systems Inc.'s.
Ascend officials did not return calls.
A UUNet spokeswoman in Fairfax, Va. said she did not have any information about an impending deal with Ascend and said nothing has been announced.
Ascend Chief Executive Mory Ejabat is believed to be travelling and meeting with investors to discuss the company's prospects.
On July 15, Ascend will report its second-quarter earnings, which will for the first time include the results of its recent merger with Cascade Communications Corp., which closed Monday.
Also on Monday, Ascend restated its first-quarter earnings to reflect the pooling of Cascade, which resulted in a loss of $163.2 million, or 88 cents a share.
